verdict: Starbucks' turnaround reached the stores — comparable sales rose 7.2% — even as revenue fell 4% to $9.1B because China is now a licensed business; profit rebounded to $677M as last year's huge restructuring bill faded.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: China converted to a licensed JV

segments.name: North America
segments.note: The U.S. and Canada — company-run and licensed coffeehouses. Comparable sales rose 7.9% as the turnaround took hold.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Everywhere else. Revenue fell 37% because China stores moved to a licensed joint venture — Starbucks now collects royalties instead of the till sales it used to book.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink products in grocery stores, including the Global Coffee Alliance with Nestlé.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Mostly unallocated corporate items that don't belong to a segment.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — down 19% YoY as the turnaround cut overhead.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment — down 17% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairments
opex.note: Closing underperforming stores under 'Back to Starbucks' — about 250 North America coffeehouses closed in the quarter. Down from $755M a year ago.

takeaways.title: North America comps snapped back
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 7.9% in North America — average ticket +5.0% and transactions +2.7% — the clearest sign yet that 'Back to Starbucks' is working.

takeaways.title: Margins rebuilt
takeaways.text: Operating margin reached 10.8%, up from 2.9% a year ago when restructuring charges peaked; excluding one-off items, the margin was 14.0%.

takeaways.title: Still growing the footprint
takeaways.text: Starbucks opened 303 net new coffeehouses in the quarter, ending with 41,607 worldwide — even while closing about 250 weak North America stores.

otherDetail: Other income of $42M, net — $105M earned from joint ventures (such as the North America Coffee Partnership) plus $58M of interest and other income, minus $121M of interest expense.
footerNote: As Starbucks reports it, operating income is $991.8M including the $104.9M of joint-venture income; in this chart that income sits in Other income so the expense lines match Starbucks' own cost breakdown exactly.
oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $273M in the quarter (store closures), versus $755M a year ago. GAAP EPS of $0.59 compares with non-GAAP EPS of $0.80, which leaves these charges out.

Revenue comparisons are distorted by China: converting company-run stores there to a licensed joint venture in Q3 FY26 removed their sales from revenue and replaced them with royalties — the main reason International revenue fell 37%.
